verdict: Structure fits the stated goals: reference, companions, integration contracts and guides are separate, and no guide depends on records. There is one concrete doc-level API misuse (local-editing), some unverified signature claims in retained-refresh, and a comparison design that is confounded by runtime diffs. The slice can merge after the blocker is fixed. It should not replace upstream yet.
blockingIssues:
local-editing.md contradicts adapters.md. `updateTitle` sets `textContent` on `

`, whose contents Lit manages through `${title}`. That destroys Lit's ChildPart markers, and adapters.md explicitly says not to 'independently replace their managed contents afterward'. Any later render (from another event, or from a reader who adds `render` to modelEvents) will fail or go stale. Browser checks that only cover typing and external `set` will not catch this. Fix: drop `updateTitle`, use `modelEvents: { 'change:title': 'render' }`, and bind the input with Lit's `live(title)`. Lit keeps the input node, so focus and selection survive. This also removes the manual DOM helper, in line with the 'no gratuitous helpers' goal.

Do not freeze the reader-comparison baseline while six runtime files differ from upstream master. Any measured difference would mix doc effects with runtime effects. Either compare both doc sets against the same candidate tarball, or split the runtime changes out of the branch first.
risks: retained-refresh asserts API details that the docs themselves don't establish here: `prepareStart(options, { signal })`, `onStart(app, options, prepareResult)`, `setView()` returning the view, and `.setStateApi()` returning the class so it can be chained. If any of these is wrong, the flagship guide teaches a wrong API. Confirm each one against the installed-fence run, not just by reading.
The top-level `await app.start()` in retained-refresh has no rejection handling, even though the prose says the caller handles a failed activation. Readers and agents will copy the unhandled form.

`require.resolve('marionette/package.json')` throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED if the package's exports map doesn't list `./package.json`, or if there is no `require`/`default` condition. Verify from an installed tarball in an ESM-only consumer.

State disposal semantics differ by adapter. With @mnjs/data, StateApi disposes owned state. With Backbone, `disposeOwned` is a no-op even for factory-owned state. XState stops owned actors. api/shared/state.md needs to state this variance, or readers will generalize from retained-refresh.

Configuration style is inconsistent. adapters.md says examples use subclasses 'to make the affected classes explicit', but both guides call the global `setDataApi`/`setDomApi`, and retained-refresh mixes global setters with a subclass `setStateApi`. Readers will not know which to use.
readme.md and api.md duplicate the class and companion listings with slightly different wording. They will drift. Keep one canonical list.
'Remaining API coverage is identified in the reference index' overpromises. api.md gives only one sentence of gaps, not a per-class coverage list.
The Morphdom example uses a fixed `id="message"`, so multiple instances produce duplicate IDs. Morphdom also matches on IDs, which makes this more than cosmetic.
In the jQuery section, 'install jQuery first and the content adapter second' reads as npm install order. It means setter order. Say 'call setDomApi with…'.
incorrectAssumptions: Passing browser checks for focus, identity and native controls does not show that the local-editing pattern is correct. The failure mode appears only on a later render.
'29 vs 58 consumer pages' is not a meaningful gap metric. Upstream pages target v4 semantics, so page count says nothing about coverage of v5 tasks. Compare by a task inventory instead.

Treating migration as one gap among several is wrong. For replacing upstream, most existing readers are v4 users, so a focused v4→v5 migration guide is a prerequisite. It is not a parallel nice-to-have.
The AI-era thesis makes runnable consumer testing central, not secondary. Without it, agents can't verify their own work from the installed docs, which undercuts the adoption goal.
missingTests: local-editing: after typing and an external `set`, force `editor.render()` and assert the preview and input still reflect the model with no Lit error. This is currently expected to fail.

retained-refresh: stop the app mid-refresh and assert no state commit; start two overlapping refreshes and assert only the second commits; use a transport that ignores abort and assert no stale commit; `start()` rejects when `prepareStart` fails and no view is shown; after restart, assert the textarea is a new node.

existing-html: `render()` after construction preserves node identity and the current `hidden`/`aria-expanded` state; `destroy()` removes the section and a click on a detached node triggers no handler; `isRendered()`/`isAttached()` are true immediately.

adapters: Lit notifyAttach/notifyDetach while `monitorViewEvents` is disabled on an ancestor, which the doc says the application must handle; jQuery-then-Lit setter order leaves jQuery `findEl` in place; Backbone multi-consumer destroy leaves survivors subscribed.
Installed-package doc lookup (`require.resolve`) from both a CJS and an ESM-only consumer.
Typecheck the TypeScript fence under the consumer tsconfig used in tooling.md, not just the repository's own config.
simplifications: local-editing: replace `updateTitle` and all manual DOM access with `render` plus `live()`, which removes about 8 lines.

retained-refresh: move the paragraphs on prepareStop, rejected stop and destruction ordering into api/application.md and link to it. The guide only needs 'onStop aborts, isCurrent guards late results'. Consider having `refresh` return nothing rather than inventing a true/false policy that the prose then has to disclaim.
adapters.md: split the combined Lit and Morphdom fence into one minimal example per adapter. Pass `message` through options/templateContext instead of assigning `lit.message` after construction.
adapters.md TypeScript fence: remove the `void actorApi` lint appeasement and the unrelated jQuery `findEl` demo. Show one typed selector example, since that is what the prose describes.
Keep a single canonical index. readme.md should link to api.md rather than repeat its tables.
nextSteps: Fix the local-editing Lit conflict and add a forced-render check to the browser suite.
Pin down the retained-refresh signatures (prepareStart context, onStart args, setView return, chained setStateApi) through the installed-fence run, and add a `.catch` to `start()`.
Choose one configuration style (global or subclass) for guides and state it once.
Priority before replacing upstream: (1) v4→v5 migration guide, (2) runnable consumer testing, (3) practical TypeScript composition, (4) production guidance, (5) external-host/router recipes.

Fair evidence of improvement: freeze both doc sets against the same rc.2 tarball. Pre-register a task set of 8–12 tasks covering migration, local edit, retained refresh, adopting HTML, adapter swap and a testing task, including tasks upstream covers and the new docs don't. Run agents and/or readers with identical retrieval (installed docs only) and blind grading. Measure task success, runtime and lint/type check pass rate, API misuse count, and time/tokens. Report tasks where the new docs lose.
